memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest shall then take some of the log of oil, pour it in the palm of his own left hand, dip his right forefinger into the oil in his palm, and with his finger sprinkle some of it before the LORD seven times." - Lev 14:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before any oil touches the person, it is sprinkled seven times before the LORD.

The direction matters. The first movement is Godward. Before this restored man is anointed, God is honoured. Seven times — completely, deliberately, unhurriedly.

We are usually in more of a rush. We want the blessing on us, and we want it now. Our prayers can become a list of needs with a brief greeting attached. But the pattern God builds into worship is always the same: He comes first.

Look at how Jesus taught us to pray. Before "give us today our daily bread," there is "hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done" (Matt 6:9-10). God's name, God's kingdom, God's will — and then our needs. Not because our needs are unimportant to Him, but because a heart that starts with God receives everything else rightly.

Oil throughout Scripture is associated with anointing and with the Spirit's presence and empowering. And notice: it goes before the LORD first. Whatever God gives us is meant to be received as something offered to Him before it is enjoyed by us.

Start Godward today. The rest will find its proper place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your prayer life begin with God or with your list?
2. What would change if you started each day Godward?
3. What blessing have you received that you have not offered back to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to begin with You. Before I ask for anything, let my heart honour Your name and seek Your kingdom above my own concerns. Amen.
